facts.fact: El Eco is a contemporary art gallery in the centre of Mexico City.
facts.quote: The Museo Experimental El Eco is a contemporary art gallery in the centre of Mexico City, Mexico.

facts.fact: In 1952 the businessman Daniel Mont commissioned Mathias Goeritz to build a place joining his restaurant-bar with the avant-garde art scene of the time.
facts.quote: In 1952, businessman Daniel Mont commissioned artist Mathias Goeritz to build a place that would articulate a new relationship between his commercial interests of a restaurant-bar and the avant-garde spirit of some cultural actors of the time, with the intention of finding something different from what was established.

facts.fact: Its corridors, ceilings, walls, rooms and openings were laid out to make visitors feel space emotionally, challenging the functionalism of the day.
facts.quote: It was designed as a poetic structure whose layout of corridors, ceilings, walls, rooms and openings led its visitors to reflect their experience of space in an emotional act; This concept challenged the dominant interests of functionalism in architecture at that time.

facts.fact: Goeritz conceived the building as a sculpture you can walk into.
facts.quote: Goeritz conceived the building as a penetrable sculpture.

facts.fact: Goeritz designed it in 1952–53 and first presented his Emotional Architecture Manifesto at its pre-inauguration in 1953.
facts.quote: In 1953, he first presented his "Manifiesto de la Arquitectura Emocional" (Emotional Architecture Manifesto) at the pre-inauguration of the Museo Experimental El Eco in Mexico City, which he designed in 1952–53.

facts.fact: UNAM bought the building in 2004 and reopened it on 7 September 2005 after restoring it to its original state.
facts.quote: In 2004, the Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México bought the building which re-opened its doors on 7 September 2005 after many months of restoration work to bring the building back to its original state.

facts.fact: Since 2008 the museum has run a national competition for young Mexican architects to build a pavilion, continuing its spatial experiments.
facts.quote: In 2008, the museum initiated a national architecture competition to continue the legacy of spatial experimentation that hosts an interdisciplinary art program. The project offers a platform for young Mexican architects and is co-produced with Buró—Buró, an independent non-profit cultural office.

facts.fact: The Teresa Carreño Cultural Complex is Venezuela's most important theatre, hosting concerts, opera, ballet and plays, and the second largest theatre in South America.
facts.quote: The Teresa Carreño Cultural Complex (Complejo Cultural Teresa Carreño), also known as Teresa Carreño Theatre (Teatro Teresa Carreño), is the most important theatre of Caracas and Venezuela, where performances include symphonic and popular concerts, opera, ballet and plays. It is the second largest theater in South America after the Néstor Kirchner Cultural Centre at Buenos Aires.

facts.fact: Pedro Antonio Ríos Reyna proposed it in the 1970s as a home for the Venezuela Symphony Orchestra.
facts.quote: In the 1970s, Pedro Antonio Ríos Reyna presented a plan to build a theatre to serve as the residence of the Venezuela Symphony Orchestra.

facts.fact: Funding came in September 1970, and the architects were Dietrich Kunckel, Tomás Lugo and Jesús Sandoval.
facts.quote: The funds for construction were granted in September 1970, and the architects were Dietrich Kunckel, Tomás Lugo, and Jesús Sandoval.

facts.fact: It opened in two phases: the José Félix Ribas Hall in February 1976 and the Ríos Reyna Hall with the rest of the complex on 19 April 1983.
facts.quote: The theatre was inaugurated in two phases: the José Félix Ribas Hall in February 1976, followed by the Ríos Reyna Hall and the rest of the complex on 19 April 1983.

facts.fact: It covers a 22,586 m² site with more than 80,000 m² of built area.
facts.quote: The Teresa Carreño Theatre is an architectonical and cultural masterpiece of Venezuela. It covers a surface of 22,586 m2 (243,110 sq ft) and has a completed area of over 80,000 m2 (860,000 sq ft).

facts.fact: The building is known for enormous columns and overlapping hexagonal roofs.
facts.quote: Enormous columns and hexagonal roofs in a harmonic overlaid position, integrate the majestic expression of joint architecture and pluralist nature, making it a unique theatre.

facts.fact: The José Félix Ribas Hall, for chamber music, takes the form of a Greek semicircular theatre seating 440.
facts.quote: It takes the form of a Greek semicircular theatre, a space of 507.5 square meters, a lobby of 160 square meters and capacity for 440 people, making it an ideal venue for chamber music, duos and solo instrument concerts.

facts.fact: Rogelio Salmona designed the Gabriel García Márquez Cultural Center in Bogotá between 2004 and 2008.
facts.quote: Gabriel García Márquez Cultural Center, Bogotá (2004–2008)

facts.fact: The SOMISA Building, officially the "Teniente General Castiñeiras" building, was the headquarters of SOMISA, Argentina's state-owned steel company.
facts.quote: The office of the Cabinet chief has two seats, one of them is located at the Somisa Building (officially known as the "Teniente General Castiñeiras" building), former headquarters of the Sociedad Mixta Siderúrgica Argentina (SOMISA), a state-owned metallurgy company created in 1972.

facts.fact: Mario Roberto Álvarez designed it in the modernist style; it was built from 1966 to 1977.
facts.quote: The building, designed in the modernist style by Mario Roberto Álvarez, was built from 1966 to 1977 and was the first building in Argentina to be made entirely out of 3 mm steel sheets and to be fully welded.

facts.fact: It was the first building in Argentina made entirely of 3 mm steel sheets and fully welded.
facts.quote: The building, designed in the modernist style by Mario Roberto Álvarez, was built from 1966 to 1977 and was the first building in Argentina to be made entirely out of 3 mm steel sheets and to be fully welded.

facts.fact: It stands on Julio Argentino Roca Avenue in the Monserrat district of Buenos Aires.
facts.quote: The building, designed in the modernist style by Mario Roberto Álvarez, was built from 1966 to 1977 and was the first building in Argentina to be made entirely out of 3 mm steel sheets and to be fully welded. It is located on Julio Argentino Roca Avenue in the Monserrat barrio of Buenos Aires.

facts.fact: After SOMISA was privatised in 1993, the government bought the building as the headquarters of the Cabinet Chief's office.
facts.quote: Following the privatization of Somisa in 1993, the building was acquired by the national government to be used as the headquarters of the newly created Cabinet Chief's office.

facts.fact: Praça das Artes is a cultural complex in São Paulo for music, dance, theatre and visual arts, opened in 2012 as an extension of the São Paulo Municipal Theater.
facts.quote: Praça das Artes is a Brazilian cultural complex located in the city of São Paulo that promotes performances and exhibitions related to music, dance, theater and visual arts. Inaugurated in 2012, it functions as an extension of the activities of the São Paulo Municipal Theater, as well as being home to the São Paulo Dance School, the São Paulo Municipal Music School, the Conservatory Hall and the Municipal Theater's artistic groups.

facts.fact: It was created to bring the Municipal Theater's artistic groups and training schools, scattered around the city centre, into one place.
facts.quote: In order to bring together all the artistic groups and training schools in a single location with adequate infrastructure, the Praça das Artes was created.

facts.fact: The design wraps around the old Conservatory of Drama and Music as a mix of building and square, reached from Avenida São João, the Anhangabaú Valley and Conselheiro Crispiniano Street.
facts.quote: The architectural project for the cultural complex aimed to create a space surrounding the São Paulo Conservatory of Drama and Music, creating a mixed form of building and square, with access from Avenida São João, Anhangabaú Valley and Conselheiro Crispiniano Street.

facts.fact: It was designed by Marcos Cartum, Marcelo Ferraz and Francisco Fanucci as an urban renewal project in central São Paulo.
facts.quote: Designed by architects Marcos Cartum, Marcelo Ferraz and Francisco Fanucci, the cultural complex established itself as an urban redevelopment intervention in the central area of São Paulo.

facts.fact: Several damaged buildings were taken over for it; the conservatory was restored and built in, and the Cairo cinema's facade was kept.
facts.quote: Several damaged buildings were expropriated for its construction, including the conservatory, which was restored and incorporated into the complex's design. The Cairo and Saci cinemas were also expropriated, but the first had its facade preserved.

facts.fact: Covering 28,500 m², it was begun in 2009 and its first part opened on 5 December 2012.
facts.quote: Occupying an area of 28,500 m2 (307,000 sq ft), construction on Praça das Artes began in 2009 and the first module was inaugurated on December 5, 2012.

facts.fact: A second phase opened on 23 March 2019, with an inner square opening onto the Anhangabaú Valley, a garden and an outdoor bar.
facts.quote: The second phase also included the inauguration of an internal square opening onto the Anhangabaú Valley, a garden and an outdoor bar.

facts.fact: It won the São Paulo Association of Art Critics' Best Work of Architecture award in 2012 and Icon's Building of the Year in 2013, and was a Mies Crown Hall Americas Prize finalist in 2014.
facts.quote: The work became a landmark in the architecture of the city of São Paulo and received the award for Best Work of Architecture in 2012 from the São Paulo Association of Art Critics, the Building of the Year award in 2013 from the Icon Awards, held by Icon Magazine, and in 2014 it was a finalist for the Impressive Projects of the Americas from the Mies Crown Hall Americas Prize.

facts.fact: The JK Bridge is a steel and concrete arch bridge across Lake Paranoá in Brasília.
facts.quote: Juscelino Kubitschek Bridge (Portuguese: Ponte Juscelino Kubitschek), commonly called Ponte JK (English: JK Bridge), is a steel and concrete arch bridge across Lake Paranoá in Brasília, Brazil.

facts.fact: It opened to traffic on 15 December 2002 and its silhouette quickly became a Brasília landmark.
facts.quote: Opened to traffic on December 15, 2002, its distinctive silhouette quickly became a Brasília landmark.

facts.fact: It was designed by architect Alexandre Chan and structural engineer Mário Vila Verde.
facts.quote: It was designed by architect Alexandre Chan and structural engineer Mário Vila Verde.

facts.fact: Chan meant the bridge to be a landmark for the community to enjoy, not only a way across the water.
facts.quote: Chan's idea for the President Juscelino Kubitschek Bridge was to create a landmark for the enjoyment of the community as much as to simply traverse a body of water.

facts.fact: The deck is carried by three 61 m tall asymmetrical steel arches that cross diagonally, on four pillars standing on the lakebed.
facts.quote: The main span structure has four supporting pillars standing on the Lake Paranoá lakebed; and the deck weight is supported by three 200-foot-tall (61 m) asymmetrical steel arches that crisscross diagonally.

facts.fact: Steel cables alternate from side to side of the deck, interlacing in a twisted plane.
facts.quote: The decks are suspended by steel cables alternating at each side of the deck, interlacing in a twisted plane.

facts.fact: The whole structure is 1,200 m long and cost US$56.8 million.
facts.quote: The entire structure has a total length of 1,200 metres (3,900 ft), and was completed at a cost of US$56.8 million.

facts.fact: Chan won the Gustav Lindenthal Medal for the bridge at the 2003 International Bridge Conference in Pittsburgh.
facts.quote: Alexandre Chan received the Gustav Lindenthal Medal for the bridge's project at the 2003 International Bridge Conference in Pittsburgh.

facts.fact: Salman Schocken commissioned Erich Mendelsohn to design Modernist buildings, starting with his chain of department stores in Germany.
facts.quote: Schocken commissioned German Jewish architect Erich Mendelsohn to design Modernist style buildings.

facts.fact: Schocken left Germany for the Holy Land in 1934 and built the Schocken Library in Jerusalem, also designed by Mendelsohn.
facts.quote: In 1934 Schocken left Germany for the Holy Land. In Jerusalem, he built the Schocken Library, also designed by Erich Mendelsohn.

facts.fact: The library was built to hold Schocken's important book collection, at what is now 6 Balfour Street, close to his home.
facts.quote: Schocken also had a library built in Jerusalem for his significant book collection. The building was also designed by Erich Mendelsohn and was built at what is now 6 Balfour Street, close to his home.

facts.fact: Today the building is home to the Schocken Institute for Jewish Research of the Jewish Theological Seminary of America.
facts.quote: Today the historic building is home to the Schocken Institute for Jewish Research of the Jewish Theological Seminary of America.

facts.fact: The institute keeps the Salman Schocken Library and other archives and collections of Jewish and other books.
facts.quote: The Institute houses the Salman Schocken Library and other important archives and collections of Jewish and other books.

facts.fact: The Wohl Centre is a convention centre on the main campus of Bar-Ilan University in Ramat Gan, Israel.
facts.quote: The Wohl Centre is a convention center on the main campus of Bar-Ilan University in Ramat-Gan, Israel.

facts.fact: Built between 2001 and 2005, it covers about 3,900 m².
facts.quote: Wohl Centre was built between 2001 and 2005 and covers about 42,000 square feet (3,900 square meters).

facts.fact: Daniel Libeskind designed it with the local firm Heder Partnership; it is noted for its stark exterior and uncluttered interior.
facts.quote: The building, designed by the internationally renowned Daniel Libeskind and a local architecture firm, the Heder Partnership, has been noted for its stark exterior and uncluttered interior.

facts.fact: It was Libeskind's first building in Israel, built on a relatively small budget.
facts.quote: The building, which was Daniel Libeskind's first in Israel, was built on a relatively small budget.

facts.fact: Three long rectangular bars form the base, and a 1,000-seat auditorium rests above them.
facts.quote: Three long rectangular "bars" comprise the building's base, above which rests a 1,000-seat auditorium.

facts.fact: Its angular form evokes an open book, meant by Libeskind to embody the link between knowledge and faith.
facts.quote: The center's angular form evokes an open book and, according to Libeskind, embodies "the interrelation between the dynamics of knowledge and the unifying role of faith."

facts.fact: Window shapes inspired by Hebrew letters cut across a gold-coloured aluminium exterior.
facts.quote: Hebrew letters inspired the shapes of the windows, which cut across a gold-colored aluminum exterior.

facts.fact: It won a RIBA International Award in 2006 and was designated a B-class conservation site in 2019.
facts.quote:
In 2006, the Wohl Centre won a RIBA International Award for its architecture.
The building was designated in 2019 a B-class site for conservation.

facts.fact: KAFD is a metro interchange in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District, serving the Yellow, Blue and Purple Lines.
facts.quote: KAFD Metro Station (Arabic: محطة قطار كافد) is a rapid transit interchange station in the al-Aqeeq neighborhood of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. It serves the Yellow Line, Blue Line, and Purple Line of the Riyadh Metro and is located within the King Abdullah Financial District.

facts.fact: Zaha Hadid Architects won the Royal Commission for Riyadh City's design competition for the station in 2013.
facts.quote: In 2013, Zaha Hadid Architects won the design competition held by the Royal Commission for Riyadh City for the KAFD metro station, which was initially expected to be completed by 2017.

facts.fact: The station covers 8,150 m² and was designed by Zaha Hadid Architects.
facts.quote: Covering an area of 8,150 square meters, the station was designed by ZHA Architects.

facts.fact: Its design draws on mashrabiya screens and the patterns desert winds make in sand dunes.
facts.quote: Its design draws inspiration from mashrabiya screens and the patterns created by desert winds in sand dunes.

facts.fact: The station has six metro tracks.
facts.quote: The station features six metro tracks.

facts.fact: Construction began in 2014; by 2019 its unclad skeleton was visible from outside.
facts.quote: Construction began in 2014, with tunneling work on the Blue Line starting in July 2015. By 2019, the exterior of the station was visible in an unclad skeletal form.

facts.fact: It earned LEED Gold certification in October 2024 and opened to the public in December 2024.
facts.quote: The station earned Gold-level LEED Certification in October 2024, and in December 2024, it was completed and officially opened to the public.

facts.fact: The Perot Museum is a natural history and science museum in Victory Park, Dallas, named after Margot and Ross Perot.
facts.quote: The Perot Museum of Nature and Science (shortened to Perot Museum) is a natural history and science museum in Dallas, Texas, in Victory Park. The museum was named in honor of Margot and Ross Perot.

facts.fact: Thom Mayne of Morphosis conceived the building as a large cube floating over a landscaped plinth.
facts.quote: Designed by Thom Mayne of Morphosis Architects, the building was conceived as a large cube floating over a landscaped plinth (or base).

facts.fact: The plinth carries a one-acre rolling green roof of rock and native drought-resistant grasses that reflects the Texas landscape.
facts.quote: The plinth was landscaped with a 1-acre (0.40 ha) rolling green roof comprising rock and native drought-resistant grasses that reflects Texas' indigenous landscape and demonstrate a living system that will evolve naturally.

facts.fact: A continuous escalator runs inside a 46 m glass tube that juts diagonally out of the cube.
facts.quote: The building is characterized by a continuous flow escalator, measuring 54 feet (16 m) in length and housed within a 150-foot (46 m) glass casing that extends diagonally outside the building cube.

facts.fact: A rainwater system collects run-off from the roof and car park, meeting 74% of the museum's non-potable water needs and all of its irrigation.
facts.quote: Building on the museum's commitment to resource conservation, the new building has a rainwater collection system that captures run-off water from the roof and parking lot, satisfying 74% of the museum's non-potable water needs and 100% of its irrigation needs.

facts.fact: Skylights bring daylight into the atrium and other spaces.
facts.quote: To enhance energy efficiency, the atrium and other spaces within the building benefit from natural sunlight via strategically placed skylights.

facts.fact: The 17,000 m² building has six floors and stands about 14 storeys high, with 11 permanent exhibit halls.
facts.quote: The 180,000-square-foot (17,000 m2) facility has six floors and stands about 14 stories high. Five of the floors are accessible to the public and house 11 permanent exhibit halls as well as 6 learning labs.

facts.fact: Donations paid for the building, with no debt or public funding.
facts.quote: The donated funds enabled the museum to be built, incurring no debt or public funding.

facts.fact: The Architecture Museum was founded by the Norwegian architects' association in 1975 and joined the National Museum on 1 July 2003.
facts.quote: The Architecture Museum was established by the Norwegian Architects National Association in 1975 and became a part of the National Museum 1 July 2003.

facts.fact: Renamed National Museum – Architecture, it opened in 2008 at Bankplassen 3 in Oslo.
facts.quote: The museum renamed the National Museum – Architecture, opened in 2008 at a new location, Bankplassen 3 in Oslo.

facts.fact: The museum is three separate buildings built together; the oldest is the former Bank of Norway branch designed by Christian H. Grosch and finished in 1830.
facts.quote: The museum is located in three separate buildings that are built together. The main building – the oldest section – was the Norges Banks Christianiaavdeling which was designed by Christian H. Grosch and was finished in 1830.

facts.fact: Sverre Fehn's addition of 2002, the Ulltveit-Moe Pavilion, sits diagonally behind the bank, with a 1911 storage building by Henry Bucher as the third part.
facts.quote: Diagonally behind is Sverre Fehns addition from 2002 – the Ulltveit-Moe Pavilion. There is also a storage building from 1911, designed by Henry Bucher.

facts.fact: Fehn's work on the National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design in Oslo dates from 2003–08.
facts.quote: 2003-08 – National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design, Oslo

facts.fact: It shows changing exhibitions of models, drawings and photographs from the collection.
facts.quote: National Museum – Architecture shows alternating exhibits from the collection that consists of models, drawing, and photographs.

facts.fact: The National Museum holds Norway's most important architecture collection, more than 300,000 items from the 1830s to today.
facts.quote: The National Museum has Norway's most important architecture collection, featuring more than 300,000 items dated from the 1830s to current day.

facts.fact: Officially the National Handicrafts and Handlooms Museum, it is one of India's largest crafts museums.
facts.quote: The National Handicrafts and Handlooms Museum (NHHM) commonly known as National Crafts Museum in New Delhi is one of the largest crafts museums in India.

facts.fact: It stands on the corner of Pragati Maidan, facing the Purana Qila.
facts.quote: The museum is situated on the corner of the Pragati Maidan, facing the Purana Quila complex.

facts.fact: Its collection of over 35,000 pieces is housed in a building Charles Correa designed between 1975 and 1990, using traditional architectural vocabulary in a modern design.
facts.quote: Today the museum holds over 35,000 rare and distinctive pieces reflecting the continuing tradition of Indian craftsmen through painting, embroidery, textiles, various crafts of clay, stone and wood, all housed in a building designed between 1975 and 1990 by architect Charles Correa, incorporating traditional architectural vocabulary into a modern design.

facts.fact: Here Correa introduced "rooms open to the sky", his systematic use of courtyards.
facts.quote: On the National Crafts Museum in New Delhi (1975–1990), he introduced "the rooms open to the sky", his systematic use of courtyards.

facts.fact: A 5-acre village complex of 15 structures shows dwellings, courtyards and shrines from different Indian states, left from a 1972 exhibition on rural India.
facts.quote: The museum also houses a village complex spread over 5-acre (20,000 m2), with 15 structures representing village dwellings, courtyards and shrines from different states of India, with items of day-to-day life displayed. The entire village complex is a remnant of a temporary exhibition on the theme of rural India, held in 1972.

facts.fact: Folk artists paint the open walls along the village complex's corridors and passages, with new artists arriving every month.
facts.quote: The Village Complex also has open walls along the corridors & passages which are used as the canvas to display the painted traditions of several tribes of folk artisans. New folk artists come in every month from different parts of the country to paint on the museum's walls.

facts.fact: In 2015 renovations whitewashed a room of Madhubani murals painted by Ganga Devi, drawing wide criticism.
facts.quote: In 2015, the Crafts Museum was renovated, and the walls painted by Ganga Devi were completely whitewashed, entirely destroying the hand-painted murals, ostensibly to remedy damage in the walls.

facts.fact: The Open Hand is a symbolic structure by Le Corbusier in Chandigarh's Capitol Complex and the emblem of the Government of Chandigarh.
facts.quote: The Open Hand Monument is a symbolic structure designed by the architect Le Corbusier and located in the Capitol Complex of the Indian city and union territory of Chandigarh. It is the emblem and symbol of the Government of Chandigarh and symbolizes "the hand to give and the hand to take; peace and prosperity, and the unity of mankind".

facts.fact: The largest of Le Corbusier's Open Hand sculptures, it stands 26 m high; its 14 m metal vane weighs 50 tons and was designed to turn in the wind.
facts.quote: The largest example of Le Corbusier's many Open Hand sculptures, it stands 26 metres (85 ft) high. The metal structure with vanes is 14 metres (46 ft) high, weighs 50 short tons (100,000 lb), and was designed to rotate in the wind.

facts.fact: For Le Corbusier the open hand was a recurring symbol of peace and reconciliation, open to give and to receive.
facts.quote: The Open Hand (La Main Ouverte) in Chandigarh is a frequent theme in Le Corbusier's architecture, a symbol for him of "peace and reconciliation. It is open to give and open to receive".

facts.fact: It stands in Sector 1 of the Capitol Complex, against the backdrop of the Shivalik hills.
facts.quote: The Open Hand is located in Sector 1 in the Capitol Complex of Chandigarh, on the backdrop of the Himalayan Shivalik hill range.

facts.fact: Le Corbusier died in 1965; the Open Hand was only built in 1985, twenty years later.
facts.quote: In spite of these efforts, it was twenty years after his death in 1965 that the Open Hand, his dream project, was realized in 1985.

facts.fact: The hand rises 26 m above a 12.5 by 9 m trench; the vane stands on a concrete platform and looks like a flying bird.
facts.quote: The Open Hand sculpture is 26 metres (85 ft) high above a trench of 12.5 by 9 metres (41 ft × 30 ft). The metal wind vane, which is erected over a concrete platform, is 14 metres (46 ft) in height and weighs 50 tons; it appears like a flying bird.

facts.fact: It was hand-cast in sheet metal at Nangal, faced in polished steel and set on a steel shaft with ball bearings so the wind can turn it.
facts.quote: The sculpture was hand-cast in sheet metal at the Bhakra Nangal Management Board's workshop at Nangal. The surface of the vane is covered with polished steel and is fitted over a steel shaft with ball bearings to facilitate free rotation by the wind.

facts.fact: The Shaheed Minar is Bangladesh's national monument to those killed in the Bengali language movement demonstrations of 1952.
facts.quote: The Shaheed Minar (Bengali: শহীদ মিনার romanised: 'Shohid Minar' lit. 'The Martyr Tower') is a national monument in Dhaka, Bangladesh, established to commemorate those killed during the Bengali language movement demonstrations of 1952 in then East Pakistan.

facts.fact: It was designed and built by the sculptors Hamidur Rahman and Novera Ahmed, delayed by martial law and completed in 1963.
facts.quote: To commemorate the dead, the Shaheed Minar was designed and built by Bangladeshi sculptors Hamidur Rahman and Novera Ahmed. Construction was delayed under martial law, but the monument was completed in 1963.

facts.fact: A half-circle of columns stands for a mother with her fallen sons on the central dais, with the red sun shining behind.
facts.quote: The enormous design includes a half-circular arrangement of columns to symbolise the mother, with her fallen sons, standing on the monument's central dais, and the red sun shining behind.

facts.fact: The marble floor was designed to show the moving shadows of the columns, and the basement held a 140 m² fresco of the language movement's history.
facts.quote: The marble floor was designed to reflect the moving shadows of the columns. The basement of the Minar also included a 1,500-square-foot (140 m2) fresco depicting the history of the language movement.

facts.fact: Rahman designed the monument's materials to withstand the area's tropical climate.
facts.quote: Rahman specifically designed the materials of the monument to withstand the area's tropical climate.

facts.fact: The Pakistan Army destroyed it during the 1971 Liberation War; it was rebuilt after independence and expanded in 1983.
facts.quote: It remained standing until the Bangladesh Liberation War in 1971, when it was completely demolished during Operation Searchlight. After Bangladesh gained independence later that year, it was rebuilt. It was expanded in 1983.

facts.fact: The hurried rebuilding got it wrong: the columns came out shorter, their heads bent more than planned, and the proportions changed.
facts.quote: Hurried repair of the Shaheed Minar resulted in the Minar to be reconstructed incorrectly. The height of the column was shorter and the head bent more than originally planned, and the proportions of different parts of the monument were not properly maintained.

facts.fact: Each 21 February, now also International Mother Language Day, national observances centre on the monument.
facts.quote: National, mourning, cultural and other activities are held each year on 21 February (Ekushey February) to mark Language Movement Day or Shaheed Dibas (Martyrs' Day), centred on the Shaheed Minar. Since 2000, 21 February is also recognised as International Mother Language Day.

facts.fact: The Jim Thompson House is a museum in central Bangkok holding the art collection of Jim Thompson, who designed it and lived there.
facts.quote: The Jim Thompson House is a museum in central Bangkok, Thailand, housing the art collection of American businessman and architect James Harrison Wilson Thompson or simply Jim Thompson, the museum designer and former owner.

facts.fact: Built in 1959, it covers about half an acre.
facts.quote: Built in 1959, the museum spans one rectangular rai of land (approximately half an acre or 2023.43 square meters).

facts.fact: Thompson began it in 1958 as a home to live in and to show his art collection.
facts.quote: In 1958, he began what was to be the pinnacle of his architectural achievement, a new home to live in and to showcase his art collection.

facts.fact: It combines six traditional Thai-style houses, mainly of wood, and other old structures gathered from around Thailand.
facts.quote: The museum was planned to consist of a complex combination of six traditional Thai-style houses, primarily constructed of wood, and various old Thai structures that were collected from all parts of Thailand in the 1950s and 1960s.

facts.fact: The house sits on the Saen Saep canal, across from Bangkrua, where his silk weavers then worked.
facts.quote: His home sits on a klong (canal) Saen Saep across from Bangkrua, where his company's weavers were then located.

facts.fact: Most of the 19th-century houses were taken apart and moved from Ayutthaya; the largest, a weaver's house that is now the living room, came from Bangkrua.
facts.quote: Most of the 19th-century houses were dismantled and moved from Ayutthaya, but the largest, a weaver's house (now the living room), came from Bangkrua.

facts.fact: The houses were brought by river and their woodwork pieced back together on site.
facts.quote: Most of the units were dismantled and brought over by river from Ayutthaya, but the largest – a weaver's house (now the living room) – came from Bangkrua. On arrival, the woodwork was offloaded and pieced together.

facts.fact: After Thompson disappeared in Malaysia in 1967, the house passed to the James H. W. Thompson Foundation.
facts.quote: After Thompson's disappearance in Malaysia in 1967, the house came under the control of The James H. W. Thompson Foundation under the royal patronage of Princess Maha Chakri Sirindhorn.

facts.fact: The Independence Monument in Phnom Penh was built in 1958 to mark Cambodia's independence from France in 1953.
facts.quote: The Independence Monument (Khmer: វិមានឯករាជ្យ [ʋimiən ʔaekariəc]) in Phnom Penh, capital of Cambodia, was built in 1958 to memorialise Cambodia's independence from France in 1953.

facts.fact: It stands on a roundabout where Norodom and Sihanouk Boulevards meet in the city centre.
facts.quote: It stands on a roundabout in the intersection of Norodom Boulevard and Sihanouk Boulevard in the centre of the city.

facts.fact: It takes the form of a lotus-shaped stupa in the style of Banteay Srei and other Khmer historic sites.
facts.quote: It is in the form of a lotus-shaped stupa, of the style seen at the temple at Banteay Srei and other Khmer historical sites.

facts.fact: Vann Molyvann designed it, chosen and instructed by Prince Norodom Sihanouk to combine the religious and the secular.
facts.quote: The Independence Monument was designed by the Cambodian architect Vann Molyvann, who was “personally selected and instructed” by Prince Norodom Sihanouk on how it should look like, combining “the religious and the secular.”

facts.fact: It stands 37 metres tall.
facts.quote: It stands 37 metres tall.

facts.fact: During national celebrations a ceremonial flame is lit on its inner pedestal and flowers line the stairs.
facts.quote: During national celebrations, the Independence Monument is the centre of activity. A ceremonial flame on the interior pedestal is often lit by a royal or high official on these occasions, and floral tributes line the stairs.

facts.fact: Molyvann is credited with modernising Phnom Penh; the monument is among his landmarks, with Chaktomuk Conference Hall and the Olympic Stadium.
facts.quote: He is credited with modernising the nation's capital Phnom Penh and designing several iconic landmarks, including the Independence Monument, Chaktomuk Conference Hall and Olympic Stadium.

facts.fact: Skidmore, Owings & Merrill designed Terminal 2 as a tribute to Bengaluru's title of 'Garden City'; Larsen & Toubro built it.
facts.quote: The airport's second terminal was designed as a tribute to the 'Garden City' title of Bengaluru by Skidmore, Owings & Merrill, and was constructed by Larsen & Toubro.

facts.fact: Work began in 2018, was delayed by the COVID-19 pandemic, and the terminal was inaugurated on 11 November 2022, opening for flights in January 2023.

facts.fact: The first phase covers 255,000 m², cost ₹5,000 crore and adds capacity for 25 million passengers a year.
facts.quote: The first phase of Terminal 2, built at a cost of ₹5,000 crore (US$520 million), is 255,000 square metres (2,740,000 sq ft) and will help augment the capacity of the airport by an additional 25 million passengers per annum.

facts.fact: A second phase is under construction to add 20 million passengers a year.
facts.quote: The second phase of Terminal 2 is under construction to increase capacity by an additional 20 million passengers per annum.

facts.fact: Arrivals are on the ground floor and departures on the first floor.

facts.fact: Since 12 September 2023 Terminal 2 has handled all of the airport's international flights.
facts.quote: On 12 September 2023, Terminal 2 began handling all international operations, with Saudia Flight 867 (SV867) from Jeddah operating the first international arrival and subsequent departure.

facts.fact: The Kigali Convention Centre is a convention centre in Rwanda's capital, Kigali.
facts.quote: The Kigali Convention Centre is a convention Centre in Kigali, the capital and largest city in Rwanda.

facts.fact: It stands on Highway KN5 by the KG2 Roundabout, about 6 km west of Kigali International Airport.
facts.quote: The convention centre is located on Highway KN5, adjacent to the KG2 Roundabout, about 6 kilometres (4 mi) west of Kigali International Airport.

facts.fact: In 2007 three Rwandan investors formed Ultimate Concept Limited to develop and own it.
facts.quote: In 2007, three Rwandan corporate investors pooled resources to build the real estate complex. They formed a company called Ultimate Concept Limited, to develop and own the centre.

facts.fact: The conference centre seats 2,600.

facts.quote: A 5-star hotel, Radisson Blu Hotel Kigali, with 292 rooms on six floors

facts.fact: Built to a design by German architect Roland Dieterle, it was begun in 2009 and completed in 2016.
facts.quote: Construction began in 2009 according to the design by German architect Roland Dieterle and was completed in 2016.

facts.quote: African Union Summit on July 8, 2016

facts.fact: The King Fahad National Library is Saudi Arabia's legal deposit and copyright library.
facts.quote: The King Fahad National Library (KFNL, Arabic: مكتبة الملك فهد الوطنية) is the legal deposit and copyright library for Saudi Arabia.

facts.fact: The library project was announced in 1983, work began in 1986 and the library opened in Riyadh in 1990.
facts.quote: The project was announced in 1983 in response to an initiative made by the people of Riyadh when King Fahd ascended the throne, and the implementation started in 1986. The library opened in Riyadh in 1990.

facts.fact: The present building is the third to house Turkey's parliament.
facts.quote: The current Parliament Building is the third to house the nation's parliament.

facts.fact: The assembly sits in a modern, monumental building in Ankara's Bakanlıklar district, designed by the Austrian architect and professor Clemens Holzmeister.
facts.quote: The Grand National Assembly is now housed in a modern and imposing building in the Bakanlıklar neighborhood of Ankara. The monumental building's project was designed by architect and professor Clemens Holzmeister (1886–1993).

facts.fact: Holzmeister's list of works dates the Grand National Assembly to 1938–1960.
facts.quote: Turkish Grand National Assembly 1938-1960

facts.fact: Before it, parliament met in Vedat Tek's building from 1924 to 1960.
facts.quote: the second building which housed the Parliament was designed by architect Vedat Tek (1873–1942) and used from 1924 to 1960.

facts.fact: After remodelling the Salzburg Festival Theatre in 1926, Holzmeister spent several years building government buildings in Ankara.
facts.quote: In 1926 he oversaw the remodelling of the Festival Theatre in Salzburg, then spent several years erecting government buildings in Ankara, Turkey.

facts.fact: The building appeared on the back of Turkey's 50,000 lira banknotes of 1989–1999.
facts.quote: The building was depicted on the reverse of the Turkish 50,000 lira banknotes of 1989–1999.

facts.fact: It was hit by airstrikes three times in the 2016 coup attempt and renovated that summer.
facts.quote: The building was hit by airstrikes three times during the 2016 Turkish coup d'état attempt, suffering noticeable damage. It went through a renovation in the summer of 2016.

facts.fact: The faculty sees itself as heir to a teaching tradition going back to 1779, and is linked to the architectural tradition known as the Porto School.
facts.quote: The faculty presents itself as the heir to a teaching tradition shared with the Faculty of Fine Arts since 1779, and it is associated with the architectural tradition known as the Porto School.

facts.fact: Its building on the Campo Alegre campus above the Douro was designed by its former teacher Álvaro Siza and built in phases from the mid-1980s.
facts.quote: Its building on the university's Campo Alegre campus, above the Douro, was designed by its former teacher Álvaro Siza and built in phases from the mid-1980s: the adaptation of the Quinta da Póvoa estate and the Carlos Ramos Pavilion, followed by a main complex formed by a northern block and four towers facing the river.

facts.fact: Siza first adapted an old estate's house and stables, and built the Carlos Ramos Pavilion (1985–86), a provisional U-shaped building around a semi-open courtyard placed among existing trees.
facts.quote: At the north-western end of the garden he built the Carlos Ramos Pavilion (1985–1986), conceived as a provisional building and organised in a U-shape around a semi-open courtyard, its placement conditioned by the existing trees.

facts.fact: A continuous string of volumes to the north holds the administration, auditorium, gallery and library and shields the courtyard from bridge traffic; four free-standing four-storey studio towers face the river to the south.
facts.quote: To the north, a continuous string of volumes – a linear block, a semicircular body and a prismatic volume – houses the administration, the auditorium, the exhibition gallery and the library and shields the courtyard from the traffic of the bridge access roads; to the south, four free-standing towers of four storeys, which hold the studios, turn their narrow fronts towards the river.

facts.fact: One tower was left out so the courtyard opens towards the Arrábida Bridge, and atria, galleries, ramps and stairs link the parts.
facts.quote: A tower was left out so that the courtyard opens towards the Arrábida Bridge, and the parts of the complex are linked by a network of atria, galleries, ramps and stairs.

facts.fact: Set on terraces held by the estate's old stone walls, the complex was described in 1995 as a kind of acropolis.
facts.quote: Set on terraces supported by the stone walls of the Quinta da Póvoa, the complex was described in 1995 as a kind of acropolis.

facts.fact: The design moved from a monumental landmark at the mouth of the Douro to a building that dissolves into its setting, letting the old gardens' greenery into public space.
facts.quote: According to the architect Manuel Montenegro, the design evolved from a monumental building that would mark the landscape of the mouth of the Douro into one that dissolves into its surroundings, letting the greenery of the former private gardens into the public space.

facts.fact: The building is one of eight works in the nomination of Siza's architecture for the UNESCO World Heritage List, which the faculty coordinates.
facts.quote: Since 2021 the faculty has coordinated the nomination "Architectural Works of Álvaro Siza in Portugal" for inscription on the World Heritage List, which includes the faculty building among eight works by the architect; in July 2025 the World Heritage Committee deferred its examination and recommended that the nomination be revised to include fewer works.

facts.fact: The Engineering Building at the University of Leicester was designed by James Stirling and James Gowan.
facts.quote: The Engineering Building is part of the University of Leicester. It was designed by the architects James Stirling and James Gowan.

facts.fact: Stirling and Gowan were commissioned in 1957; the design dates from 1959 and it was built from 1960 to 1963, with Frank Newby as structural engineer.
facts.quote: Stirling and Gowan were commissioned in 1957. The design is dated to 1959. Construction lasted from 1960 to 1963. The consulting structural engineer was Frank Newby.

facts.fact: Low workshops sit in a rectangular hall, joined to a tower holding the auditorium, offices and laboratories, with a water tank on top.
facts.quote: The workshops are located in the low-rise section of the building, in a hall with a rectangular floor plan. Connected to the workshop hall is the tower, which houses auditorium, offices, and laboratories. The water tank sits on top of the tower.

facts.fact: The sloping floor of the auditorium shows on the outside as a pronounced wedge shape.
facts.quote: The angled auditorium floor results in a pronounced wedge-shape on the building's exterior.

facts.fact: The tower is clad in glass and red tiles; the workshop hall is entirely frosted glass.
facts.quote: The tower's facades are clad in glass and red tiles, the workshop hall's facade is entirely made of frosted glass.

facts.fact: The workshop roof is turned 45 degrees to the plan, giving a jagged roofline of translucent prisms.
facts.quote: The roof's geometry is rotated by 45 degrees in respect to the floor plan's orientation. This results in a unique jagged roof line and a diamond-pattern-like perimeter. The roof appears as a series of multiple translucent prisms.

facts.fact: It is the first of Stirling's Red Trilogy of university buildings in red brick and tile, followed by the Cambridge History Faculty and Oxford's Florey Building.
facts.quote: The Red Trilogy includes the Engineering Building, University of Leicester (1959–1963), the Seeley Historical Library, Faculty of History, University of Cambridge (1964–1967), and the Florey Building, Queen's College, Oxford (1966–1971).

facts.fact: It marks Stirling's first step from brutalism towards postmodernism and is seen as one of the origins of postmodern architecture.
facts.quote: The Engineering Building represents Stirling's first step from brutalism towards postmodernism. Therefore, the building is regarded as one of the origins of postmodern architecture.

facts.fact: In a later refurbishment its leaky steel-framed single glazing was replaced, with English Heritage approval, by aluminium double-glazed units.
facts.quote: The leaky single glazed steel framed glazing was replaced with English Heritage approval with aluminium framed double-glazed units.

facts.fact: The building is protected with a Grade II listing.
facts.quote: The building is a protected heritage site with a Grade 2 listing.

facts.fact: Behruz and Altuğ Çinici won the competition for the Middle East Technical University campus in 1961.
facts.quote: Their collaboration led to a first-place victory in the Middle East Technical University (METU) Campus Competition in 1961.

facts.fact: The faculties they designed on the campus include the Faculty of Architecture.
facts.quote: The faculties they designed include the Faculty of Administrative Sciences, Faculty of Architecture, Faculty of Science, Faculty of Education, Faculty of Engineering, and Faculty of Agriculture.

facts.fact: Behruz Çinici described their campus design as a challenge to the International Style.
facts.quote: Behruz Çinici described their approach to the METU campus design as a challenge to the International Style of architecture, which was prevalent in architectural theory, education, and culture at the time.

facts.fact: Rather than reshaping the land, their scheme grew out of many site visits and close study of the terrain.
facts.quote: Rather than modifying the landscape to suit their design, their proposal emerged from extensive site visits and thoughtful consideration of the terrain.

facts.fact: On the campus they used a 'piece construction' system and chose durable, often uncoated materials over easily damaged coatings.
facts.quote: During their work on the Middle East Technical University (METU) campus in Ankara from 1961 to 1980, Behruz Çinici and Altuğ Çinici utilized the 'piece construction' system. This approach features structural components that are both divisive in design and inclusive in installation functions. Instead of opting for easily damaged coatings, they frequently selected durable, often uncoated materials.

facts.fact: The Çinicis pioneered bare concrete techniques in Turkey, first developed at METU.
facts.quote: The Çinici duo pioneered the use of bare concrete techniques in Turkey, first developed at the METU campus.

facts.fact: They moved their office to Ankara in 1962 and Behruz Çinici worked mainly on the METU campus until 1980.
facts.quote: Subsequently, they relocated their workshop to Ankara in 1962, where Çinici focused primarily on designing structures for the METU campus until 1980.

facts.fact: Glenn Murcutt's list of works dates the Magney House at Bingie Bingie, New South Wales, to 1982–1984.
facts.quote: 1982–1984: Magney House, Bingie Bingie (NSW)

facts.fact: In 2011 it won the New South Wales and National Awards for Enduring Architecture.
facts.quote: 2011: New South Wales Enduring Architecture Award and National Award for Enduring Architecture for Magney House, Bingie

facts.fact: Following the park's World Heritage listing, a building was built with a museum showing many artefacts found in the park.
facts.quote: With the park's UNESCO World Heritage status, a building has been constructed that houses a museum section with many of the artefacts uncovered in the park on display.

facts.fact: The Museum and Interpretive Centre also gives information on the park's history and biology.
facts.quote: Information on the park's history and biology is also available at the Museum and Interpretive Centre.

facts.fact: The Mapungubwe Interpretation Centre is by Peter Rich Architects and was named World Building of the Year at the World Architecture Festival.
facts.quote: World Building of the Year (Category: Culture, Completed Buildings ) Mapungubwe Interpretation Center in South Africa by Peter Rich Architects

facts.fact: The building won World Building of the Year at the 2009 World Architecture Festival.
facts.quote: In 2009, the building won the World Architecture Festival's World Building of the Year.

facts.fact: The Mannheim Multihalle, by Frei Otto with Arup, is a very large exhibition space built in 1975.
facts.quote: Mannheim Multihalle by Frei Otto and Arup Structures 3 (many of whose team members later left to found Buro Happold), a very large exhibition space constructed in 1975.

facts.fact: Its timber gridshell was built by laying the laths out flat in a square lattice and pushing them up from the ground into a doubly curved form.
facts.quote: Large span timber gridshells are commonly constructed by initially laying out the main lath members flat in a regular square or rectangular lattice, and subsequently deforming this into the desired doubly curved form. This can be achieved by pushing the members up from the ground, as in the Mannheim Multihalle.

facts.fact: Frei Otto's list of works dates the Multihalle in Mannheim to 1975.
facts.quote: 1975 – Multihalle, Mannheim, Germany

facts.fact: The museum in Marrakesh is dedicated to the fashion designer Yves Saint Laurent.
facts.quote: The Yves Saint Laurent Museum in Marrakech (Arabic: متحف إيف سان لوران بمراكش, French: Musée Yves Saint Laurent de Marrakech, stylized mYSLm) is a museum dedicated to the fashion designer Yves Saint Laurent located in Marrakesh, Morocco.

facts.fact: Pierre Bergé said it was natural to build it in Morocco, since Saint Laurent's colours and forms owe so much to the country.
facts.quote: According to Pierre Bergé, the designer's business partner and onetime life partner, "it was natural to build a museum dedicated to the work of Yves Saint Laurent in Morocco, as he—even in the colors and the forms of his clothing—owes so much to the country."

facts.fact: It opened to the public on 19 October 2017 and won Wallpaper's best new public building award in 2018.
facts.quote: It was inaugurated October 2017 and opened to the public 19 October 2017. In January 2018, the museum received the best new public building award at the 2018 Design Awards of the British international design magazine Wallpaper.

facts.fact: It stands on Rue Yves Saint Laurent, near the Majorelle Garden.
facts.quote: This Marrakesh museum is located on a street that had already been named after the designer, Yves Saint Laurent Street, near Majorelle Garden—Saint Laurent's residence in Morocco, transformed since his death into a garden, a Berber Art Museum, and an exhibition space that received more than 700,000 visitors per year.

facts.fact: The 4,000 m² museum was designed by Studio KO and built by the Moroccan arm of Bouygues.
facts.quote: The museum covers an area of 4,000 m2 (43,000 sq ft). It was designed by Studio KO and built by the Moroccan subsidiary of Bouygues.

facts.fact: Outside, the earth-coloured building is an assemblage of cubes and curves wrapped in a lace of brick that evokes woven fabric.
facts.quote: From the exterior, the earth-colored building takes the form of an assemblage of cubes and curves, dressed in a lace of bricks evoking weaves of fabric.

facts.fact: It is built of terracotta, concrete and terrazzo in colours that blend with the surroundings; the earth bricks were made locally from Moroccan earth.
facts.quote: The materials are terra cotta, concrete, and terrazzo, with colors allowing the building to blend in with its surroundings. The earth bricks were made from Moroccan earth and produced locally.

facts.fact: Besides the Saint Laurent hall it has a hall on Jacques Majorelle, temporary exhibition halls and a 130-seat auditorium.
facts.quote: Another hall is dedicated to Jacques Majorelle, there are temporary exhibition halls, and holds an auditorium with 130 seats.

facts.fact: Notre-Dame du Raincy is a Catholic church near Paris, built in 1922–23 by Auguste and Gustave Perret.
facts.quote: The Église Notre-Dame du Raincy (Church of Notre Dame du Raincy) is a Roman Catholic church in the commune of Le Raincy near Paris. It was built in 1922-23 by the French architects Auguste Perret and Gustave Perret.

facts.fact: It is seen as a monument of modernism, using reinforced concrete to show what the new material could do.
facts.quote: The edifice is considered a monument of modernism in architecture, using reinforced concrete in a manner that expresses the possibilities of the new material.

facts.fact: The parish priest proposed it in 1918 to commemorate the French victory at the Battle of the Marne in 1914.
facts.quote: In 1918, the parish priest of Le Raincy, Felix Nègre, proposed to build a church to commemorate the French victory in the Battle of the Marne in 1914.

facts.fact: Concrete was chosen for economy and used on its own terms, not to imitate masonry: standard elements, slender supports and thin membranes pierced by windows.
facts.quote: The design used concrete for economy. Rather than attempting to simulate masonry, the new material was used on its own terms, with standardized elements, slender supports, and thin membranes pierced by windows.

facts.fact: The non-load-bearing outer walls are made of square precast concrete panels pierced with geometric openings that hold the glass.
facts.quote: The perimeter walls are non-load-bearing and assembled from square precast concrete panels, or claustra, pierced with geometrical openings that carry the glazing; a limited number of standardized patterns is combined across the building.

facts.fact: Marguerite Huré's stained glass runs from blues near the entrance to warmer tones in the sanctuary.
facts.quote: The stained glass was created by Marguerite Huré using colored coatings on clear glass for economy. The colors are dominated by blues near the entry and progress to warmer tones in the sanctuary.

facts.fact: Inside, the columns were left undecorated and the concrete ceiling vaults became the main decoration.
facts.quote: He also created innovative industrial buildings, including a warehouse in Casablanca covered with a think veil of concrete (1915); the Perret Tower, the first concrete tower for the International Exhibition of Hydropower and Tourism of Grenoble (1925), to demonstrate his "Order of Concrete"; and the church of Notre Dame du Raincy (1922–23), where the interior columns were left undecorated and the concrete vaults of the ceiling became the most prominent decorative feature.

facts.fact: Listed as a historic monument in 1966, it has had two restorations since 1990, the later one using newer methods for repairing reinforced concrete.
facts.quote: The church was listed as a historic monument in 1966. Two programmes of conservative restoration have been undertaken by Caisse Nationale des Monuments Historiques since 1990, the more recent benefitting from developments in technique for restoring reinforced concrete and its steel reinforcements.

facts.fact: It houses the common High Court of Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh.
facts.quote: Punjab and Haryana High Court is the common High Court for the Indian states of Punjab and Haryana and the Union Territory of Chandigarh based in Chandigarh, India.

facts.fact: The court building, known as the Palace of Justice, was designed by Le Corbusier and inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in July 2016 with several of his other works.
facts.quote: The court building is known as the Palace of Justice. Designed by Le Corbusier, it and several of his other works were inscribed as UNESCO World Heritage Sites in July 2016.

facts.fact: Le Corbusier, who made the master plan for Chandigarh, was chosen to build the high court, and Prime Minister Nehru took a close interest in the project.
facts.quote: Le Corbusier, who designed the master plan for Chandigarh, was chosen to execute the project of building the high court. India's first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, enthusiastically supported the project and took a sustained interest in its execution.

facts.fact: Visiting in 1952, Nehru called Chandigarh a new town symbolic of India's freedom, unfettered by the past.
facts.quote: When he visited the project on 2 April 1952, he declared "Let this be a new town symbolic of the freedom of India, unfettered by the traditions of the past, an expression of the nation's faith in the future."

facts.fact: The court moved to its present home in Chandigarh on 17 January 1955.
facts.quote: From 17 January 1955, the Court was moved to its present location in Chandigarh.

facts.fact: The listing covers seventeen Le Corbusier projects in seven countries, as an outstanding contribution to the Modern Movement.
facts.quote: In 2016, seventeen projects by Le Corbusier in seven countries were inscribed in the list of UNESCO World Heritage Sites as The Architectural Work of Le Corbusier, an Outstanding Contribution to the Modern Movement.

facts.fact: Ando's housing at Rokko, just outside Kobe, is a warren of terraces, balconies, atriums and shafts.
facts.quote: Ando's housing complex at Rokko, just outside Kobe, is a complex warren of terraces and balconies, atriums and shafts.

facts.fact: Rokko Housing One (1983) and Two (1993) play solid against void, open against closed, and light against dark.
facts.quote: The designs for Rokko Housing One (1983) and for Rokko Housing Two (1993) illustrate a range of issues in traditional architectural vocabulary—the interplay of solid and void, the alternatives of open and closed, the contrasts of light and darkness.

facts.fact: The clustered buildings survived the 1995 Great Hanshin earthquake undamaged.
facts.quote: More significantly, Ando's noteworthy engineering achievement in these clustered buildings is site-specific—the structures survived undamaged after the Great Hanshin earthquake of 1995.

facts.fact: The Rokko apartments, with the Church of the Light, earned Ando international recognition.
facts.quote: The Rokko apartments and the Church of the Light earned Ando international recognition, and he was noted by those who detect a regional quality in concrete construction.

facts.fact: Aldo Rossi won the 1971 competition to extend the San Cataldo Cemetery in Modena, which made him internationally famous.
facts.quote: In 1971, he won the design competition for the extension of the San Cataldo Cemetery in Modena, which made him internationally famous.

facts.fact: It shows Rossi's repetitive postmodernist design, and drew the common criticism that his work put "monumental collectivity" above the individual.
facts.quote: The work was representative of Rossi's repetitive postmodernist design, but was also representative of a common objection to Rossi's work: that it focused too much on "monumental collectivity" over individualism.

facts.fact: It is Rossi's largest project, begun in 1971 and still not completed.
facts.quote: The largest of Rossi's projects in terms of scale was the San Cataldo Cemetery, in Modena, Italy, which began in 1971, but is yet to be completed.

facts.fact: Rossi called it a "city of the dead".
facts.quote: Rossi referred to it as a "city of the dead".

facts.fact: Rossi's list of works gives the ossuary and cemetery as 1971–1984.
facts.quote: 1971–1984 Ossuary and the Cemetery of San Cataldo in Modena

facts.fact: The SPACE Group building (1978) is listed among Kim Swoo-geun's representative works, which feature Korean traditional elements.
facts.quote: His representative works include "SPACE Group building" (공간 사옥, 1978), "Masan Yangdeok Catholic Church" (마산양덕성당 1979), "Jinju National Museum" (진주국립박물관 1986) and "Olympic Main Stadium" (올림픽 경기장 1987), which feature his characteristic view of architecture as well as Korean traditional elements.

facts.fact: The building stands in Wonseo-dong, Jongno District, Seoul; Kim's list of works dates it to 1971.
facts.quote: 1971 SPACE Group Building (공간 사옥) in Wonseo-dong, Jongno District, Seoul

facts.fact: In 1978 Kim set up SPACE Love, a small theatre inside the building, which played a role in South Korean cultural life.
facts.quote: Kim also established SPACE Love (공간사랑) in 1978, a small theater inside of the Space group building and built the SPACE Gallery in 1972, all of which has played an important role for numerous South Korean cultural campaigns.

facts.fact: Takasugi-an, in Chino, Nagano, is a tea house of four and a half tatami mats raised six metres above the ground on two load-bearing trees; its name means "too high tea house".
facts.quote: Situated in Chino in Nagano Prefecture, the Takasugi-an Tea House is a four and a half tatami mat tea house supported six metres above the ground on two load-bearing trees (the name literally means "too high tea house").

facts.fact: Instead of stooping through a low entrance as in a traditional tea house, the visitor climbs a ladder to the top.
facts.quote: Rather than using the traditional method of entering a tea house by stooping low, the visitor climbs a ladder to the top.

facts.fact: Fujimori replaced the hanging scroll that marks the season with a large window framing the town where he grew up.
facts.quote: For example, the picture scroll (kakejiku) that normally gives a clue about the time of year is replaced with a large window that frames a view to the town where Fujimori grew up.

facts.fact: It stands on two chestnut trees cut and brought from a nearby mountain.
facts.quote: It is supported on two chestnut trees that were cut and moved to the site from a nearby mountain.

facts.fact: Fujimori's work is known for humour, experimental natural materials and twisting traditional techniques.
facts.quote: His architecture is characterised by eccentricity and humour, experimental use of natural materials and the subversion of traditional techniques.

facts.fact: It was built in 2003–2004.
facts.quote: Takasugi-an Tea House (2003–2004)

facts.fact: The Vidhan Bhavan houses the Madhya Pradesh Legislative Assembly, the state's single-chamber legislature.
facts.quote: The Madhya Pradesh Legislative Assembly is the unicameral state legislature of Madhya Pradesh state in India.

facts.fact: It stands at the centre of the Capital Complex on Arera Hill in Bhopal.
facts.quote: It is housed in the Vidhan Bhavan, an imposing building located at the center of the Capital Complex in the Arera Hill locality of Bhopal city.

facts.fact: Charles Correa designed the building in 1967; it won the Aga Khan Award for Architecture in 1998.
facts.quote: The present building was designed by Charles Correa in 1967, and it was the recipient of the Aga Khan Award for Architecture in 1998.

facts.fact: It was one of Correa's first significant projects, following the Gandhi memorial at Sabarmati Ashram.
facts.quote: His first significant project was the Mahatma Gandhi Sangrahalaya (Mahatma Gandhi Memorial) at Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad (1958–1963), followed by the Madhya Pradesh Legislative Assembly in Bhopal (1967).

facts.fact: The award was given in the 7th cycle of the Aga Khan Award for Architecture.

facts.fact: The assembly it houses has 230 directly elected members.

facts.fact: Skogskyrkogården, the Woodland Cemetery south of central Stockholm, opened in 1920 and became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1994.
facts.quote: Skogskyrkogården ([ˈskûːɡsɕʏrkʊˌɡoːɖɛn]; Swedish for 'The Woodland Cemetery') is a cemetery located in the Gamla Enskede district south of central Stockholm, Sweden. It was inaugurated in 1920 and was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1994.

facts.fact: Its design by Gunnar Asplund and Sigurd Lewerentz traces architecture's move from Nordic Classicism to mature functionalism.
facts.quote: Its design, by Gunnar Asplund and Sigurd Lewerentz, reflects the development of architecture from Nordic Classicism to mature functionalism.

facts.fact: After changes asked for by the competition jury, work began in 1917 on old gravel quarries overgrown with pines; the first phase was finished three years later.
facts.quote: After changes made to the design on the recommendations of the competition jury, work began in 1917 on land that had been old gravel quarries that were overgrown with pine trees, and the first phase was completed three years later.

facts.fact: Their use of the natural landscape created a calm setting that deeply influenced cemetery design worldwide.
facts.quote: The architects' use of the natural landscape created an extraordinary environment of tranquil beauty that had a profound influence on cemetery design throughout the world.

facts.fact: A long route from the entrance splits: one way past a pond and a tree-lined meditation hill, the other up to a large granite cross and the crematorium's portico.
facts.quote: The basis for the route through the cemetery is a long route leading from the ornamental colonnaded entrance that then splits, one way leading through a pastoral landscape, complete with a large pond and a tree-lined meditation hill, and the other up to a large detached granite cross and the abstract portico of the crematorium and the chapels of the Holy Cross, Faith, and Hope.

facts.fact: The architects designed everything from the landscape to the smallest lamp; Lewerentz mainly did the landscape, the main entrance and the Resurrection Chapel (1925).
